children: said Thursday it lifted the force majeure on its Tennessee Gas Pipeline after repairs restored natural gas shipments to Mexico that had been interrupted earlier in the week.

Tennessee Gas has resolved problems that were identified on October 5 that forced the company to isolate and shut some sections of pipe, including the Rio Bravo and Cenagas delivery meters, according to a filing, and the company declared force majeure the following day.

Mexico is the largest buyer of U.S. pipeline gas, with ~75% of the country's gas coming from Texas, and American pipeline exports to Mexico have surged to ~8 Bcf/day from ~1 Bcf/day in 2010, according to BloombergNEF data.
Mexico does not have large-scale underground storage comparable to the U.S., leaving its power sector heavily dependent on continuous pipeline deliveries from the north.
In the event of outages, Mexico only has about three days of gas supplies in reserves, according to Cuitlahuac Garcia, director of Mexican pipeline operator Cenagas.

title: Kinder Morgan restores natural gas flows to Mexico after pipeline outage
